content: De-identified Clinical Note (MIMIC-style synthetic). Patient: 72-year-old female with atrial fibrillation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, GERD, and osteoarthritis. Current medications: warfarin 5mg daily (INR target 2.0-3.0), metformin 1000mg BID, lisinopril 20mg daily, atorvastatin 40mg daily, omeprazole 20mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50mg daily, amlodipine 5mg daily. Presenting complaint: prescribed clarithromycin 500mg BID for community-acquired pneumonia. Risk assessment: HIGH risk regimen. Critical interaction: clarithromycin (strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) will increase atorvastatin exposure 4-fold, risk of rhabdomyolysis. Clarithromycin also increases warfarin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, risk of bleeding. Omeprazole has minor effect on warfarin R-enantiomer metabolism. Recommendation: Switch to azithromycin (no CYP3A4 inhibition), or reduce atorvastatin to 10mg and increase INR monitoring frequency to every 2-3 days during antibiotic course.
